chapter_note: Overwhelmingly substrate chapter. The teaching describes three conduits (lihme) connecting heavenly powers to earthly domains, through which life ascends and waste descends. The entire cosmological architecture—conduits, roots, the wheel of stars, the Ambassador myth, cosmic geography—maps domain to domain without ever reaching into the contemporary world. No editorial bridge, institutional, or exhortation vocabulary detected at all. The only later material consists of thin dialogue frame formulas wrapping the teaching. The Persian dialogue tradition is strong here: the disciples' questions about zodiacal authority and conduit hierarchy reveal teaching structure. Heavy lacunae in the later paragraphs (22-24) but the surviving words are consistently cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: There are three conduits that exist through the entire zone, from the abyss to its heights.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Once again the enlightener speaks:' — formulaic dialogue frame attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Frame formula 'Once again the enlightener speaks' wraps a concise cosmological proposition defining the three conduits and their scope (abyss to heights). The teaching statement is the kernel of the entire chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: The first conduit is the root of all the powers above, they that exist in all the heavens. They are cast off and fettered on the earths below; because the earth below is the 'stripping off', the garment and the body of the powers that are above the heavens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pure correspondential teaching. The earth IS the body/garment of the heavenly powers. Both sides of the mapping are cosmic domains. 'Stripping off' is technical cosmological vocabulary for the divestment process.

paragraphs.core_text: For when the Father of Life constructed the heavenly worlds, he divested them of their bodies, [he] threw them to the earths below.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological process narrative. 'Father of Life' is a cosmic agent (the Living Spirit). Describes the construction event that established the conduit system.

paragraphs.core_text: So, the upper worlds are of the soul and the spirit; but the worlds below are of the body and the carcass [...] ⟨p.121⟩ Now as for this, he [...] the powers of heaven; he sealed it on their bodies and their carcasses that are on the earths, so that when life comes up from the fullness of these earths, it can be entirely drawn up to the heights in the roots of what is heavenly, that are fastened in their bodies. And also, all life can be purified in that place.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic degree-mapping: upper worlds = soul and spirit, lower worlds = body and carcass. This is classic correspondential substrate—the psychic/pneumatic vs. somatic/ptomatic distinction mapped onto cosmic geography. The conduit mechanism (life drawn up through roots) is pure cosmological process.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the waste that will be swept from the purified one who ascends to the heights will be let fall to the ground through the conduits of these conduits, and will be poured down [...] and thrown to the underside.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes the descending function of the conduit system. Purification process: life ascends, waste descends. Both directions stay within the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: This is the first conduit, which comes from the powers of the heavens to their bodies and their carcasses that are upon the earth; also, from their bodies and [their] carcasses that are on the earths to the powers of the heavens.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Summary of the first conduit. Bi-directional mapping: heavenly powers ↔ earthly bodies/carcasses. Pure cosmic system description.

paragraphs.core_text: The second conduit is the one that comes from the temples and dwellings and cities that exist in the heavens down to the ground, to the five shapes of tree that grow upon the earth. The life comes up from the trees to the temples and cities. Life too, and the residue of the heavenly ones, comes down to the trees in a conduit.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second conduit maps HEAVENLY temples/cities → five shapes of tree. 'Temples and dwellings and cities' are cosmic structures in the heavens, not earthly institutions. 'Five shapes of tree' is systematic five-element nomenclature applied to vegetation. Both sides cosmic.

paragraphs.core_text: And the third conduit is all the powers and householders who dwell in all the firmaments, whose roots come down from them to the five worlds of flesh that creep upon the earth, being fixed to one another. Now, the power and the life that shall be gathered in from the worlds of flesh are dispersed among them in various shapes. The powers above shall draw them to the upper side through conduits.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third conduit: firmament powers → five worlds of flesh. 'Householders' are cosmic rulers, not human inhabitants. 'Five worlds of flesh' is systematic five-element nomenclature. The dispersal and gathering mechanism is pure cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: [The was]te too, and the lust and the evil-doing and the anger that will be greater in the powers of [heave]n, shall be poured to the ground through their various conduits. They shall be discharged upon mankind and the other remaining animals. When what is heavenly will wash the waste and the stench and the poison down on the creations of the flesh below, in their turn the creations shall be greater in lust and anger and evil-doing against each other through the action of their fathers who are on high.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Describes cosmic determinism through the descending conduit. 'Mankind' here is a category of the five worlds of flesh (cosmic taxonomy), not a contemporary audience. Lust, anger, evil-doing are cosmic qualities poured down from 'fathers who are on high'—heavenly powers. Both sides of the mapping remain cosmic. No exhortation or application.

paragraphs.core_text: Still, look at the wheel of the stars! It has no [root in this earth], but its roots are bound in the totality. The wheel of stars, then, receives life through the power and the life that ascend from the earths through conduits and the firmaments above. It (also) takes life from those conduits that receive up to the firmaments and the heavenly worlds above it, it takes life out from that place.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'The apostle says:' — dialogue frame attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Teaching about the wheel of stars and its unique rootedness. Unlike the three conduits, the wheel has no root in earth but draws life from the conduit system itself. 'Look at the wheel of the stars!' is pedagogical voice, not frame—it directs attention to a cosmic object.

paragraphs.core_text: In that the wheel has no root in this earth, from where did the stars and signs of the zodiac find this authority? They became masters over these five fleshes and five trees. Every thing, if it can be reduced from the earth, the heavenly powers above draw it through a conduit. Also, every thing that a person will attain, whether it be wealth that comes into his possession or poverty that will accrue to him, or his sickness and health; he attains it through the signs of the zodiac and the star under which he shall be born.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Then the disciples questioned the enlightener. They say to him: Look,' (dialogue frame attribution), 'Even though you have told us that the wheel has no root there! For you said to us that' (retrospective dialogue references), and 'we see that' (dialogue observational voice).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question in the Persian pedagogical tradition. The paradox—the wheel has no earthly root yet controls earthly fate—defines the teaching problem that paragraphs 12-16 resolve. The question about zodiacal authority over five fleshes and five trees uses systematic nomenclature. The observation about wealth, poverty, sickness, health is cosmological determinism, not contemporary application.

paragraphs.core_text: the wheel has no root therein. It is set aright in its position. For when the Living Spirit, the Father of Life, constructed the heavens and the firmaments above, he bound their roots into the earths below; in their carcasses that he had stripped from them. Yet, when he constructed the wheel, [he] did not bind its root into the earths, but he bound the root of the wheel by the sea giant.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'Then he says to his disciples: Nevertheless, what I proclaimed to you, namely that' (dialogue frame attribution and retrospective reference) and 'I have recounted to you properly.' (dialogue self-reference).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core teaching distinguishes the wheel's binding from the firmaments' binding. The wheel is bound to the sea giant, not to the earths. The Living Spirit's construction sequence is cosmic process narrative. 'Sea giant' is a cosmic entity (cf. chapter 44).

paragraphs.core_text: And when [the] Ambassador came, he displayed his image and purified and brought the light out from all [the] heavens. Matter, however, which is present in all the rulers, spurted out against the image of the Ambassador. It went up in order to reach it, but reached it not. It dropped back and fell to the [under]side. Now, when it had fallen from above, it separated out into three parts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The Ambassador myth—a core cosmological narrative. The Ambassador displays his image, Matter in the rulers ejaculates upward, fails to reach the image, and falls in three parts. This is cosmic process description, not historical narrative. 'Ambassador' and 'Matter' function as cosmic agents.

paragraphs.core_text: The first part fell to the wheel; another part fell to the earth; an[other part fell to the se]a. ⟨p.123⟩ [By means] of the part that fell to the sphere, [the r]oot was bound in the trees and flesh. Therefore, because of this, they received authority and became masters in the five worlds of the flesh and the five worlds of the tree.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Three-fold distribution of fallen Matter: wheel, earth, sea. The sphere's portion established the root binding zodiacal authority to vegetation and flesh. 'Five worlds of the flesh and the five worlds of the tree' is systematic five-element nomenclature. This resolves the paradox raised in paragraph 11.

paragraphs.core_text: Through the nature that came down [upo]n the wheel the root was bound in the trees. Also, by means of the abortions that came to the ground, another root was bound in the fleshes.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Further specification of the binding mechanism: fallen nature → trees, abortions → fleshes. Two distinct root-binding events. 'Abortions' is technical cosmological vocabulary for the demonic spawn that fell to earth.

paragraphs.core_text: Therefore, because of this, the stars and signs of the zodiac received authority over the trees and the fleshes: through the root of Sin that fell down; and [the ro]ot of the abortions that were aborted there, they fell to the ground.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seam flag is a false positive—the 'institutional vocabulary' field is empty. 'Therefore, because of this' is a logical connective summarizing the cosmic process of paragraphs 13-15. Content is entirely cosmological: zodiacal authority derived from the root of Sin and abortions. Both sides cosmic. Sin capitalized as personified cosmic agent.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the[se] other conduits that [the] Living Spirit has bound in the e[a]rths, they that the soul of the elements comes up through to the heavens; those (conduits) are not bound to the wheel. Rather, they are plundered from them by the powers on the wheel, that hang from it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Critical distinction: the three conduits are NOT bound to the wheel—they are plundered by the wheel's powers. The Living Spirit bound the conduits in the earths. 'Soul of the elements' is technical substrate vocabulary for the light trapped in matter.

paragraphs.core_text: The first is the one that comes from the firmaments to the earths, and the one that comes from the wheel to the sea giant. That is only one. So, the other root is the one that comes [fr]om [the temples] to the trees. The third is bound by means of the abortions in the f[leshes]; also in the fleshes the fathers of the abortions who are in the heavens [...] are bound and twined, and the [y] that [...]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'The disciples of the enlightener say: We beseech you, our master, that just as you have instructed us and put together this lesson on [...] you have told us about the prototype of the conduits.' (dialogue frame with honorific and retrospective reference to lesson).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive recapitulation of the three conduits by the disciples—reveals the teaching structure. This is the Persian pedagogical pattern: disciples demonstrate comprehension by restating the system. The enumeration (first, other, third) and the cosmic mappings are substrate. Heavy lacunae at the end.

paragraphs.core_text: about the conduits, the one that is greater than its [partn]er [...] as more life and soul is drawn [...] than its partner.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'We entreat you, our master, that you might instruct us [...]' (dialogue frame with honorific petition formula).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question about the hierarchy of conduits by volume of life drawn. This question defines the teaching topic for paragraphs 20-22. Fragment survives through lacunae but the structural content is clear.

paragraphs.core_text: great [...] the earth from which much life ascends [...] the Father of Life has drawn them. ⟨p.124⟩ He has fastened them from the powers [...] he has bound them in the earths. (These conduits) are the roots of the ent[ire] ruling-power that the life of the living soul is drawn up through, it coming up from the whole earth, from all the mountains, fields and islands.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'The enlightener [says] to his disciples: You have inquired about a [...] and you have asked about this lesson in superiority,' (dialogue frame attribution and retrospective reference to the disciples' question).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The first conduit is greatest because it is bound in all the earths. 'Mountains, fields and islands' is cosmic geography—all terrestrial domains from which life ascends. The Father of Life is a cosmic agent. Heavy lacunae but surviving words are consistently cosmological.

paragraphs.core_text: After that first great root is the root of the trees, which is bound to the temples and the buildings above. For there also is much great life coming up from the tree and the entire Cross, being drawn up from them to the upper side like a great host.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second conduit ranked: trees bound to heavenly temples/buildings. 'The entire Cross' is the Cross of Light—a cosmic entity referring to the light trapped in all vegetation across the earth, not the Christian cross. The image of life 'drawn up like a great host' describes cosmic process.

paragraphs.core_text: What, however, is lesser [...] of their conduit [...] he takes up [...] the roots [...] the earths, they [...] the whole earth in all the worlds. Again, these of the trees are present in the whole earth, whether small or great; but the root of mankind [...] is not present in the whole earth, other than only this world of the south. Therefore, even now these fleshes do not make [...] in the entire world of the south [...] there is a small part of them in [...] of the upper side of the world of the south in [...] in number than the [...]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third conduit is least because flesh only covers part of the world. 'World of the south' is cosmic geography—the inhabited portion of earth in the Manichaean cosmological scheme. Trees cover the whole earth but flesh only a small part. Despite heavy lacunae, every surviving word describes cosmic spatial distribution.

paragraphs.core_text: they are bound by their [roots ...] with one another. They stir one another, they draw life from one another through the action of the powers above, which stirs the nature that dwells in them all.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed 'I have instructed you about the roots [...] them, [I] have taught you that' (first-person retrospective dialogue frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological summary of the conduit system's mutual interdependence. The three conduits are bound together and exchange life through the action of heavenly powers. 'The nature that dwells in them all' is substrate vocabulary for the cosmic mixture.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, when the Matter that is in them will be crushed and despoiled, then that Matter too shall [...] its members and overturn them and [...] each other [...] stir [...] ⟨p.125⟩
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological cosmological process—the final crushing and despoiling of Matter. Despite heavy lacunae, surviving words describe cosmic process. Matter is a personified cosmic agent. This appears to be the chapter's conclusion describing the end-state of the conduit system.
